title: Optical studies of negative g-factor dopants in an antiferromagnet: Nd:GdVO$_4$
authors: Lachlan W. Cronin, Masaya Hiraishi, Luke S. Trainor, Jevon J. Longdell
abstract: Neodymium-doped gadolinium vanadate (Nd:GdVO$_4$) is a popular laser material at room temperature. It has received limited attention for quantum technologies because of the linebroadening effects of disordered gadolinium spins in the host. Here we investigate the optical properties at temperatures below the 2.5 K Néel temperature, revealing narrow optical transitions. We demonstrate that rare earth ions in magnetic hosts give us a new way of observing the signs of magnetic g-factors. The interplay between the exchange and Zeeman interactions means that we see clear evidence of negative g-factors. These results provide a detailed spectroscopic foundation for Nd:GdVO$_4$ and expand the understanding of its candidacy as a material for hybrid quantum systems.
summary: This paper uses polarization-resolved optical spectroscopy on Nd:GdVO4 to study its electronic structure across different magnetic phases. By analyzing the field-dependent absorption spectra, the authors successfully demonstrated the existence of negative magnetic g-factors. These findings significantly advance the understanding of Nd:GdVO4's potential use in hybrid quantum systems.
main_problem: The study aims to investigate the optical properties of Nd:GdVO4, specifically to observe and characterize the signs of magnetic g-factors.
main_result: The research successfully demonstrated clear evidence of negative g-factors in the system, providing a detailed spectroscopic foundation for Nd:GdVO4.
method: Polarization-resolved absorption spectroscopy was performed on Nd:GdVO4 across varying magnetic fields and temperatures.
model_or_system: The physical system is Nd-doped gadolinium vanadate (Nd:GdVO4), an antiferromagnet. The analysis employs an expanded Crystal-Field-Theory (CFT) model incorporating Zeeman, exchange, and mean-field interactions.
key_observables: The sign of the magnetic g-factor, the evolution of the 4F3/2 energy manifold, and polarization-dependent absorption spectra ($\sigma$ and $\pi$).
important_parameters: Temperatures below the 2.5 K Néel temperature, magnetic fields up to 3 T, and the interplay between exchange and Zeeman interactions.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the host lattice has D2d point symmetry, and the Nd3+ ion is treated as a Kramers ion.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the magnetic phase diagram (AFM, SF, PM). Figure 5 shows overlaid $\sigma$- and $\pi$-polarized absorption spectra in the AFM regime, fitted with the CFT model for two nonequivalent Nd sites.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the magnetic phases (AFM, SF, PM) via the magnetic field dependence, then using polarization-resolved spectroscopy to probe the electronic transitions, and finally applying CFT modeling to extract fundamental parameters like the g-factor.
why_interesting: The ability to use optical spectroscopy to map out magnetic phase transitions and extract fundamental magnetic parameters like g-factors in a solid-state rare-earth magnet is highly relevant for understanding spin dynamics in quantum materials.
